# Load packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(robotstxt)
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(viridis)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```


# Import "rawData" into this qmd file
```{r}
dataset <- load("data/rawData.Rdata")
```

# Import "stadiums-geocoded" into this qmd file (used for geospatial map)
```{r}
coordinates <- read.csv("data/stadiums-geocoded.csv")
```

# Geospatial Wrangling for Comparing Student Aid
# Convert city_txt to city in df
# Use left_join() to combine "df" with "coordinates"
# Get ratio between men/women aid
```{r}
# Rename city
aid_geospatial <- df |>
  #just wanting NCAA Division 1 -FBS
  # (NCAA A)
  filter(ClassificationCode == "1") |>
  # Rename columns to use left_join()
  rename(city = city_txt) |>
  rename(state = state_cd) |>
  left_join(coordinates, by = c("city", "state")) |>
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  drop_na(latitude) |>
  drop_na(longitude) |>
  distinct(institution_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(institution_name,
         EFMaleCount,
         EFFemaleCount,
         STUDENTAID_MEN,
         STUDENTAID_WOMEN,
         STUDENTAID_TOTAL,
         latitude,
         longitude) |>
  # Calculate ratio between men and women aid to get a proportion
  # First calculate how much money athletes are receiving PER PERSON
  # If proportion is greater than 1, than men have more aid than women
  # If proportion is less than 1, than women have more aid than men
  mutate(male_money_per_capita = STUDENTAID_MEN / EFMaleCount,
         female_money_per_capita = STUDENTAID_WOMEN / EFFemaleCount,
         male_female_aid_ratio = male_money_per_capita / female_money_per_capita
  )
```

# Geospatial Wrangling for Comparing Head Coach Salaries
# Use similar process from aid_geospatial to create new dataset
```{r}
# Create new dataset
HDCOACH_salary_geospatial <- df |>
  # just wanting NCAA Division 1 -FBS
  # (NCAA A)
  filter(ClassificationCode == "1") |>
  # Rename columns to use left_join()
  rename(city = city_txt) |>
  rename(state = state_cd) |>
  left_join(coordinates, by = c("city", "state")) |>
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  drop_na(latitude) |>
  drop_na(longitude) |>
  distinct(institution_name, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  # Filter desired columns
  select(institution_name,
         NUM_HDCOACH_MEN,
         NUM_HDCOACH_WOMEN,
         HDCOACH_SALARY_MEN,
         HDCOACH_SALARY_WOMEN,
         STUDENTAID_TOTAL,
         latitude,
         longitude) |>
  # Calculate ratio between men and women aid to get a proportion
  # If proportion is greater than 1, than men have more aid than women
  # If proportion is less than 1, than women have more aid than men
  mutate(male_coach_salary_per_capita = HDCOACH_SALARY_MEN / NUM_HDCOACH_MEN,
         woman_coach_salary_per_capita = HDCOACH_SALARY_WOMEN / NUM_HDCOACH_WOMEN,
         male_female_salary_ratio = male_coach_salary_per_capita / woman_coach_salary_per_capita)
```



```{r}

# Comparing Gender Spending Ratios Across NCAA Divisions

# Our goal is to compare gender differences in athletic spending
# between NCAA Division I-FBS and Division III institutions.
# We calculate each school's ratio of men's athletic expenses
# to women's athletic expenses, then compare the divisions.


# ClassificationCode 1 represents NCAA Division I-FBS.
division1 <- filter(df, ClassificationCode == 1)

# ClassificationCodes 6 and 7 represent Division III institutions
# with and without football, respectively.
# We include both because we want to study all Division III schools.
division3 <- filter(df, ClassificationCode == 6 |
                        ClassificationCode == 7)


# Calculating the spending ratio for each institution.


# Dividing men's expenses by women's expenses tells us how
# many dollars a school spends on men's athletics for every
# dollar it spends on women's athletics.
# We exclude schools with missing or zero women's expenses
# because a valid ratio cannot be calculated for them.

division1 <- filter(division1,
                    !is.na(IL_EXPENSE_MENALL),
                    !is.na(IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL),
                    IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL > 0)

division3 <- filter(division3,
                    !is.na(IL_EXPENSE_MENALL),
                    !is.na(IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL),
                    IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL > 0)

# creating a new column named spending_ratio using mutate.
# A ratio of 1 means equal spending on men's and women's programs.
# A ratio greater than 1 means higher spending on men's programs.
# A ratio below 1 means higher spending on women's programs.

division1 <- mutate(division1,
                    spending_ratio = IL_EXPENSE_MENALL /
                                     IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL)

division3 <- mutate(division3,
                    spending_ratio = IL_EXPENSE_MENALL /
                                     IL_EXPENSE_WOMENALL)


# Summarizing the spending ratios for each division.

# The median represents the middle spending ratio among schools.
# We use the median to compare typical institutions without
# allowing unusually large ratios to dominate the comparison.


division1_summary <- summarise(
  division1,
  schools = n(), # n() counts the institutions included in each calculation.
  median_ratio = median(spending_ratio)
)

division3_summary <- summarise(
  division3,
  schools = n(),
  median_ratio = median(spending_ratio)
)


division1_summary
division3_summary
```


# Wrangling Code for Box Plot Analysis
```{r}
#| label: Salary Comparison Coaches

coach_box_plot <- df|>
#just wanting NCAA Division 1 -FBS
# (NCAA A)
filter(ClassificationCode == "1") |>
  rename(Men_Salary = HDCOACH_SALARY_MEN,
         , Women_Salary = HDCOACH_SALARY_WOMEN) |>
select(
#school name, head coach salaries
  institution_name
  , Men_Salary
  , Women_Salary)

# wrangle more for box-plot
coach_box_plot <- coach_box_plot|>
  pivot_longer(cols = c (Men_Salary, Women_Salary)
, names_to = "Gender", values_to = "Salary")

```

```{r}
#| label: Student Aid Comparison

# data points for student aid comparison
aid_box_plot <- df|>
filter(ClassificationCode == "1") |>
  rename(Men_Aid= STUDENTAID_MEN,
         , Women_Aid = STUDENTAID_WOMEN) |>
select(institution_name, Men_Aid, Women_Aid)

# wrangle more for box-plot
aid_box_plot <- aid_box_plot|>
  pivot_longer(cols = c (Men_Aid, Women_Aid)
, names_to = "Gender", values_to = "Student Aid")

```

```{r}
#| label: Recruitment Cost Comparison

# data points for recruitment spending comparison
recruitment_box_plot <- df |>
filter(ClassificationCode == "1") |>
 rename(Men_Recruitment= RECRUITEXP_MEN,
         , Women_Recruitment = RECRUITEXP_WOMEN) |>
select(institution_name, Men_Recruitment, Women_Recruitment)

# wrangle more for box-plot
recruitment_box_plot <- recruitment_box_plot|>
  pivot_longer(cols = c (Men_Recruitment, Women_Recruitment)
, names_to = "Gender", values_to = "Recruitment")

```

# Save all datasets into one big R file
```{r}
save(aid_geospatial, HDCOACH_salary_geospatial, division1, division3, coach_box_plot, aid_box_plot, recruitment_box_plot, file = "data/wrangledData.Rdata")
```
